item: source candidate B: closure follow-through ledger

accepted_source.title: Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure (Google SRE Workbook, ch. 10)
accepted_source.tier_rationale: primary, vendor-authoritative (Google's own workbook), verbatim-fetchable stable URL, byte-hashed at open
accepted_source.scope: Google SRE's postmortem action-item ownership, tracking-bug and closeout semantics

primary_quote.text: Without a formal tracking process, action items from postmortems are often forgotten, resulting in outages.
primary_quote.verification: byte-exact in fetched HTML via grep -o

supporting_quotes.text: Ideally, an owner is a single point of contact who is responsible for the postmortem, follow-up, and completion.
If you reward engineers for writing postmortems, but not for closing the associated action items, you risk an unvirtuous cycle of unclosed postmortems.
To our users, a postmortem without subsequent action is indistinguishable from no postmortem.

not_claimed: not about code-review or verification-fixture ledgers; incident-postmortem ops context only, transfer is our analogy
no tool mandate: implies a bug tracker via the Tracking Bug column but names no product
no verifiable state machine: closeout is cultural (FixIt weeks, leaderboards), no open/closed statuses or evidence links
no quantified effect of tracking: the satellite-drain anecdote is a single case, not a measurement
no close-before-publish requirement: the good example publishes with open tracked items; the lane's tree-agreement rule is stricter

rejected_candidate.title: Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure (Google SRE Book, ch. 15)
rejected_candidate.sounds_relevant_because: identical chapter title to the preferred candidate; canonical postmortem-culture text

disqualifying_quote.text: Once those involved are satisfied with the document and its action items, the postmortem is added to a team or organization repository of past incidents.
disqualifying_quote.verification: byte-exact in fetched HTML via grep -o
disqualifying_quote.why_disqualifying: gates the document on reviewer satisfaction and a repository; no per-item owner, no tracked-to-closure state

corroborating_absence: review criteria list contains only 'Is the action plan appropriate and are resulting bug fixes at appropriate priority?' (13 words, tag-stripped verify) — review-time adequacy, no closure tracking
case-insensitive sweep: every readable 'track' token on the page is the next chapter's title 'Tracking Outages' (TOC + footer nav)
rejected_candidate.flip_condition: the Book page gains action-item ownership/tracking/closure text (the Workbook already carries it)

alternate_supporting.title: Postmortems (Atlassian Incident Handbook)
alternate_supporting.quote: All postmortem actions must be tracked in Jira.
alternate_supporting.verification: tag-stripped verify (responsive markup duplicates it twice in one HTML)
alternate_supporting.disposition: supports the claim; held as alternate row so the round opens one row per scout seat
